review_evidence: Codex self-review: safety-theme fidelity, original scenarios, evidence-backed reasoning, contextual grammar, and age-appropriate own-words tasks
Focused checks: canonical hash, key-option consistency, stage and assessment freshness, skill coverage, and chapter/corpus quality
title: Be Smart, Be Safe
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Find the safety message and proof
levels.focus: identify a safety paragraph's main idea and supporting evidence
levels.teaching_goal: State the broad safety message and use an action or consequence as evidence.

guided_check.teaching_block: The main idea joins all details. Stopping, checking traffic, and crossing at the marked place all support one message: plan before crossing.
guided_check.passage: At the corner, Veer stopped behind the kerb. He looked right, left, and right again, waited for the road to clear, and crossed at the zebra crossing.
guided_check.prompt: What is the paragraph mainly teaching?
options: Check carefully before crossing a road.
accepted_answers: Check carefully before crossing a road.

bridge.teaching_block: List the action and its purpose. Holding the rail and keeping the aisle clear both reduce danger on a bus.
bridge.passage: Mitali held the bus rail and kept her bag away from the aisle while the vehicle moved.
bridge.prompt: Which result do both actions support?

masterclass.teaching_block: A striking detail is not always the main idea. The red light is one clue; the paragraph is broadly about obeying signals before moving.
masterclass.passage: The signal turned red. Cyclists stopped behind the line, pedestrians waited on the pavement, and traffic from the other road moved.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer includes all the details?
options: Road users follow signals to move safely.
The signal has a red lamp.
The pavement is beside a road.
accepted_answers: Road users follow signals to move safely.

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the unseen paragraph and select evidence yourself.
independent_check.passage: Before skating, Arjun checked the straps, tightened his helmet, and moved stones away from the practice area. He began only when the path was clear.
independent_check.prompt: State the main safety idea and support it with one action.

concept_slots.description: states that preparation or checks make skating safer
mentions straps, helmet, stones, or clear path

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply main-idea reading to safety at home.
transfer_check.passage: Before using a mixer, Auntie unplugged it, dried her hands, fitted the jar, and called an adult to check the lid. Only then did she connect the plug.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain the main safety message in your own words and cite one detail.

concept_slots.description: states that electrical appliances require careful preparation and adult checking
uses one action from the passage

levels.title: Read signs through words and setting
levels.focus: infer public sign meanings from context
levels.teaching_goal: Use a sign's wording, location, and nearby action to infer what it requires.

guided_check.teaching_block: A sign's location is a context clue. 'No entry' beside a repair gate means people must not use that route.
guided_check.passage: Workers have opened a drain beyond a gate marked NO ENTRY.

bridge.teaching_block: Connect the command word to the danger. Caution asks people to be alert because a hazard is nearby.
bridge.passage: A yellow board says CAUTION: WET FLOOR beside a freshly mopped corridor.
bridge.prompt: What does caution tell walkers to do?

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not interpret a symbol without its setting. A crossed-out horn outside a hospital means do not sound the horn, not that vehicles are banned.
masterclass.passage: A sign outside a clinic shows a horn with a red line through it.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the wording and place in this fresh sign.
independent_check.passage: A board beside a steep staircase reads USE HANDRAIL.
independent_check.prompt: What does handrail mean in this instruction?
accepted_answers: the rail to hold while using the stairs
a support rail beside the stairs
support to hold on the stairs

transfer_check.teaching_block: Interpret a warning in a park rather than on a road.
transfer_check.passage: A rope surrounds a young tree, and a sign says FRAGILE ROOTS: KEEP OFF THE SOIL.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain what fragile means and what visitors should do.

concept_slots.description: explains that the roots are delicate or easily damaged
says to stay off or not step inside the roped area

levels.title: Judge actions by their consequences
levels.focus: infer why an action is safe or unsafe and explain the likely result
levels.teaching_goal: Use because, but, or so to connect a safety choice with evidence and consequence.

guided_check.teaching_block: A safety reason links action to consequence. 'Do not chase the ball because a driver may not see you' explains the danger.
guided_check.passage: A ball rolls towards the street while traffic is moving.
guided_check.prompt: Which reason best explains why a child should stop at the gate?
options: A driver may not see a child running out.
accepted_answers: A driver may not see a child running out.

bridge.teaching_block: Use because before a cause and so before a result.
bridge.passage: Rohan wore reflective strips _____ drivers could see him in the evening.
bridge.prompt: Which connector completes the visibility result?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common error is calling an action safe only because no accident happened. Judge the risk: looking at a phone while cycling is unsafe even if the road seems empty.
masterclass.passage: The lane looked empty, but Isha kept reading a message while cycling.
options: It is unsafe because she is distracted.
It is safe because no car is visible.
It is safe because the message is short.
It is unsafe because bicycles are blue.
accepted_answers: It is unsafe because she is distracted.

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain the consequence in this new case without choices.
independent_check.passage: Nakul waits for the bus on the pavement instead of standing on the road.

concept_slots.description: states that he is on the pavement or away from traffic
explains that vehicles are less likely to hit or endanger him

transfer_check.teaching_block: Judge risk during a storm rather than near traffic.
transfer_check.passage: Lightning begins while children are playing in an open field, so their coach leads them into a solid building.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain why the coach's action is safer.

concept_slots.description: identifies lightning or exposure in the open field
explains that the building provides shelter or reduces risk

levels.title: Use nouns and verbs in safety instructions
levels.focus: identify word jobs and countable nouns in contextual instructions
levels.teaching_goal: Use sentence meaning to distinguish objects, actions, and countable safety equipment.

guided_check.teaching_block: In an instruction, the action word tells what to do. 'Fasten the strap' uses fasten as the verb.
guided_check.passage: Fasten the helmet strap before the ride.

bridge.teaching_block: A countable noun can be counted separately. You can count cones: one cone, three cones.
bridge.passage: The instructor placed four cones around the wet patch.

masterclass.teaching_block: Some words change jobs with context. 'Signal' is a naming word in 'the signal changed' but an action in 'signal before turning.'
masterclass.prompt: What job does signal do here?

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the whole instruction before naming the word job.
independent_check.passage: Carry two bottles of water on the hike.
independent_check.prompt: Write the action word and the counted noun.

concept_slots.description: identifies carry as the action
identifies bottles as the counted noun

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use grammar clues in a laboratory instruction.
transfer_check.passage: Place three goggles beside the sink and wipe each lens.

levels.title: Write practical safety advice
levels.focus: summarise a hazard and write complete safety guidance in own words
levels.teaching_goal: Describe a hazard, give a specific action, and explain the protection it provides.

guided_check.teaching_block: Useful advice names a hazard and a protective action. Worked example: 'The floor is slippery, so walk slowly and use the rail.'
guided_check.passage: Rainwater has gathered on the school steps.
guided_check.prompt: Which message gives specific safety advice?
options: The steps are wet, so hold the rail and walk slowly.
The steps are made of stone.
accepted_answers: The steps are wet, so hold the rail and walk slowly.

bridge.teaching_block: Build advice in three parts: hazard, action, benefit. Start by identifying what could cause harm.
bridge.passage: A charging cable lies across a doorway.
bridge.prompt: What hazard should the advice mention?
options: Someone could trip over the cable.
accepted_answers: Someone could trip over the cable.

masterclass.teaching_block: Vague advice such as 'be careful' does not tell the reader what to do. Choose an observable action matched to the hazard.
masterclass.passage: A cupboard door is open above a busy passage.
options: Close the cupboard door before someone walks into it.
accepted_answers: Close the cupboard door before someone walks into it.

independent_check.teaching_block: Create the message without borrowing a model sentence.
independent_check.passage: A cyclist's backpack strap hangs close to the rear wheel.
independent_check.prompt: In two complete sentences, describe the hazard and give protective advice.

concept_slots.description: states that the loose strap may catch in the wheel
says to secure, tie, shorten, or tuck the strap before riding
expresses hazard and action as complete ideas

transfer_check.teaching_block: Write advice for handling information safely.
transfer_check.passage: A game asks a child to post a home address in a public chat to claim a prize.
transfer_check.prompt: Summarise the risk and give safe advice in your own words.

concept_slots.description: states that sharing a home address publicly exposes private information
says not to post it and to ask a trusted adult
connects the action to privacy or protection

items.passage: Before the boat trip, Zoya checked her life jacket, tightened its straps, and listened to the guide.
items.prompt: Which main idea covers all actions?
options: Preparation makes the boat trip safer.
accepted_answers: Preparation makes the boat trip safer.

items.passage: At a campsite, children cleared dry leaves from the cooking area, kept water nearby, and asked an adult to light the stove.
items.prompt: State the safety message and one supporting action.

concept_slots.description: states that careful preparation prevents fire danger
mentions one campsite action

items.passage: Mehul tests the bicycle brakes before riding downhill.
items.prompt: What can a reader reasonably infer?
options: He wants to know the bicycle can stop safely.
He plans to carry the bicycle.
accepted_answers: He wants to know the bicycle can stop safely.

items.passage: A family stores medicines in a high locked cabinet and keeps the key with an adult.
items.prompt: Explain why these details support one safety idea.

concept_slots.description: states that medicines should be kept away from children or used with adults
uses high cabinet, lock, or adult-held key as evidence

items.passage: A board beside a loose bridge plank reads DANGER: DO NOT CROSS.
items.prompt: What does danger signal?

items.passage: A bottle label says DILUTE WITH WATER BEFORE USE.
items.prompt: Use the instruction to explain dilute.

items.passage: A trail marker says STEEP DESCENT for the next kilometre.
items.prompt: Which meaning fits descent?

items.passage: A packet says PERISHABLE: KEEP REFRIGERATED.
items.prompt: What clue suggests perishable food can spoil?

items.passage: The path was icy, _____ the walkers shortened their steps.
items.prompt: Choose the result connector.

items.passage: Asha switches off the fan before cleaning its blades.
items.prompt: Explain why this choice lowers risk.

concept_slots.description: mentions switching off the fan before cleaning
explains that moving blades could injure her

items.passage: The crossing guard raised a stop sign _____ children were entering the road.
items.prompt: Which connector introduces the cause?

items.passage: The sun was strong, so the hikers wore hats and carried water.
items.prompt: Give the hazard and the protective response.

concept_slots.description: identifies strong sun or heat
mentions hats and/or water
connects response to protection

items.passage: Secure the two buckles before climbing.
items.prompt: Which word is the action?

items.passage: The guide packed three torches and extra food.
items.prompt: Write the noun directly counted by three.

items.passage: Drivers signal before changing lanes.
items.prompt: What job does signal do?

items.passage: Lift four boxes and stack them by the wall.
items.prompt: Write both action words.

items.passage: A saucepan handle points beyond the edge of a stove.
items.prompt: Which advice is specific and useful?
options: Turn the handle inward so nobody knocks it.
accepted_answers: Turn the handle inward so nobody knocks it.

items.passage: A child is about to open a link sent by an unknown account.
items.prompt: Describe the risk and give safe advice.

concept_slots.description: states that an unknown link may be harmful or deceptive
says not to open it and to ask or report
expresses both ideas clearly

items.passage: A loose tile sticks up in a busy corridor.
items.prompt: What should a pupil do first?
options: warn others and tell an adult
accepted_answers: warn others and tell an adult

items.passage: Smoke enters a room from an unknown source.
items.prompt: In your own words, state the hazard and a safe response.

concept_slots.description: identifies smoke, fire, or breathing danger
says to leave safely and alert an adult or emergency help
does not suggest investigating alone
